name: Lipoatrophy with Diabetes, Leukomelanodermic Papules, Liver Steatosis, and Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
aliases: Syndromic Lipoatrophy with Metabolic and Cardiac Involvement
Lipoatrophic Diabetes Syndrome with Dermatological and Hepatic Manifestations

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Syndromic Diagnostic Criteria for Lipoatrophy with Metabolic and Cardiac Features

criteria.description: Presence of generalized or partial lipoatrophy confirmed by clinical examination and imaging
Diagnosis of diabetes mellitus, typically insulin-resistant type
Characteristic leukomelanodermic papules distributed on the skin
Evidence of liver steatosis on imaging or biopsy
Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy confirmed by echocardiography or cardiac MRI

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: lipoatrophy, diabetes mellitus, and leukomelanodermic papules
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Additional supportive findings such as liver steatosis and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy strengthen diagnosis but are not mandatory.

pathognomonic.notes: Loss of subcutaneous fat tissue visible on clinical examination
searchTerms: thin or sunken appearance due to fat loss

pathognomonic.notes: Mixed hypopigmented and hyperpigmented papular skin lesions
Typically requiring high doses of insulin or oral hypoglycemics

common.notes: Enlarged liver with fatty infiltration detected by imaging
searchTerms: big liver due to fat accumulation

common.notes: Thickened ventricular walls with preserved systolic function
Hyperpigmented velvety plaques typically in intertriginous areas

occasional.notes: Mild to moderate elevation of ALT and AST
Shortness of breath related to cardiac involvement
Sensory deficits or paresthesias in distal extremities

rare.notes: Occasional episodes of atrial or ventricular arrhythmias
Secondary to advanced liver steatosis or fibrosis
Mild thyroid hormone deficiency reported in some cases

laboratory: Elevated fasting blood glucose and insulin resistance markers
imaging: Abdominal ultrasound or MRI demonstrating liver steatosis
MRI or CT confirming loss of subcutaneous fat tissue
genetic: No specific gene identified; possible autosomal dominant or sporadic inheritance pattern
other: Skin biopsy showing leukomelanodermic papules with mixed pigmentary changes
Electrocardiogram may show arrhythmias or conduction abnormalities

distinguishingFeatures: Congenital onset with near-total absence of adipose tissue
Severe insulin resistance and diabetes from infancy

redFlags: Rapid progression of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with heart failure symptoms
Severe insulin resistance refractory to standard diabetes treatment
Development of portal hypertension or liver failure
